title: The first proper drink
text: Someone older has pushed a plastic cup into your hand at a party. 'Go on,' they say. 'Everybody does.'

choices.label: Take a sip and put it down

outcomes.text: It tasted terrible. I felt oddly grown-up for about four minutes.
It tasted like the inside of a cough bottle. I kept the cup all night.
The room tilted pleasantly. By midnight I was the funniest person alive. By morning, I was not.
I threw up in a hedge. Someone held my hair.
Nobody cared as much as I'd feared. A girl said she was impressed.
They teased me. It faded.

title: Pub night
text: Thursday means the pub, which means a quiz team and a pint. The third pint arrives without being ordered.

outcomes.text: We came second. I walked home clear-headed.
We came last. I laughed all the way home anyway.
A great night, a bad morning.
I got into an argument about geography. I was wrong, loudly.
My team teased me and then forgot. Nobody minded.
The quiz master gave me a free orange juice. Chivalry.

title: Messages at 2 a.m.
text: You wake up with your phone in your hand, and the sick lurch of a feeling that you've sent something.

outcomes.text: It was a long, soppy message to an ex. They hadn't replied. A small mercy.
It was to my boss. It just said 'I love you man'. He sent a thumbs-up.
It was too late; they'd seen it. I apologised in the morning.
I deleted it, then checked, and found it hadn't sent. I breathed.
I really did, for about nine days.
I did, and I told someone. It helped.

title: The keys in your hand
text: It's one a.m. You've had four drinks and you feel fine. The taxi queue is long, and your car is just around the corner.

outcomes.text: It cost forty dollars and a hundred percent of my anxiety. Worth it.
It took an hour. I got home. Nothing happened. That's the point.
I got home. I did not sleep. I thought about every moment of the drive.
Blue lights in the mirror. A breath test. I failed it.
It was cold, but I was safe. A little foolish, mostly sensible.
A police officer tapped on the window at 3. She was kind about it.

title: The Monday after
text: You wake up on the sofa fully clothed, and it takes a beat to remember there's a presentation at nine. The room is far too bright.

outcomes.text: I got through it, grey and polite. Nobody noticed. I swore off drink for a whole week.
The boss smelled it. He said nothing, which was worse.
I slept until two, ate toast, and felt almost human. The guilt was bearable.
I called in sick. A colleague saw my photos from Saturday. Awkward.
I told my boss the truth. He laughed and said 'been there'. It was strangely bonding.
I told my boss. He didn't laugh. I got a quiet note on my file.

title: The toast
text: At a wedding, the champagne has been flowing for hours, and the best man has just handed you the microphone. 'Say something!'

outcomes.text: I spoke about the couple and meant every word. The room went soft.
I lost the thread, wept openly, and got a standing ovation.
It brought the house down. The groom pretended to hate me.
It was a bit too embarrassing. The groom's mother left.
Someone else took it. I had a quiet drink and felt fine.
I regretted it all evening.

title: Gaps in the night
text: You wake up in a place you don't recognise with a stranger's coat over you and no memory of the last five hours.

outcomes.text: A friend filled in the blanks. I'd been charming, apparently, and had lost a shoe.
The night had a darker shape. I'd said things. I owed apologies.
I got a taxi home. The shame lasted a week.
I found my phone, my wallet, my keys. A miracle.
I really meant it. The first month was hard.
I told a friend. She made me promise. It helped.

title: Dry month
text: A friend challenges you to a month without alcohol, for charity. The pledge sheet is on the fridge, and you've already signed it.

outcomes.text: I felt a bit better, slept well and saved a lot. I was surprised.
It was a hard month, but I did it. We raised eight hundred dollars.
I had one. Then three. The sheet stayed on the fridge.
I told them and paid up anyway. It was honest.
Nobody remembered by Wednesday.
I felt bad. The charity could have used it.

title: An intervention
text: Your family are sitting in your kitchen, holding letters. Your sister says, 'We love you. We're worried.' You can see their faces and you can see a bottle on the shelf.

outcomes.text: It was the hardest hour of my life. I started a programme the following Monday.
I agreed. I relapsed. But I'd started, and they didn't give up.
I walked out, furious. I didn't speak to my sister for a year.
They gave me space. It hurt them more than me.
We held each other. I made a promise and kept it, one day at a time.
I cried. I promised. I didn't keep it.

title: Christmas party
text: The firm's Christmas party has an open bar and a boss who has loosened his tie. A senior partner has just put a glass in your hand.

outcomes.text: Charming, sociable, and out by ten. I made a good impression.
I had a decent time and woke up fresh.
I danced on a table. It will never be forgotten.
I told the CEO exactly what I thought. In detail. In front of everyone.
I was the designated driver for four colleagues. They loved me.
I was teased, and then forgiven.

title: The long afternoon
text: It's a rare hot day. Friends, a beer garden, and no plans until tomorrow. Someone is ordering the next round.

outcomes.text: There's no such thing, but I enjoyed the lie.
Three more, and an ill-advised karaoke. I'll never speak of it.
I walked home in the golden light. A perfect afternoon.
I left, and the party got better. FOMO is real.
I stayed clear, and remembered every joke.
I became the designated one. It's a role, and I liked it.

title: Blood results
text: The doctor has the results of your routine blood test and is looking at you over the top of her glasses. 'Let's talk about your liver.'

outcomes.text: I cut back, started walking, and the next test was better. A real turning point.
I cut back for a while. It crept up again.
I told her it was a bad week. She wrote something on the chart.
A year later it was worse.
A support group on Tuesday nights. A dozen strangers, one very good coffee urn.
The first meeting was awkward. The second was better.

title: A year clean
text: Today is the day. One year without a drink. You've got a keyring chip in your hand and a lump in your throat.

outcomes.text: My sponsor hugged me. I cried in a good way.
I told my family. They were so proud it hurt.
A big mug of tea and a long walk. A lovely day.
I stared at the bottle shop on the way home and kept walking.
I held a glass at a party and put it down. Proud and shaky.
I tested it too soon. Not a good idea.

title: Last orders
text: At closing time a man steps on your foot, loudly blames you, and squares up. His friends are fanning out behind him.

outcomes.text: I walked out into the cold air feeling both a coward and a genius.
They followed, but a bouncer stopped them. I owe that man a beer.
It ended badly. I lost a tooth and a night in the cells.
A short brawl, a bloody nose and a lot of regret.
It worked, to my own amazement. We shook hands.
It didn't. I got hit anyway.

title: Hosting a dinner
text: Eight guests, a six-course menu, and the wine. The bottle of nice red is gone. Your guests are in great voice.

outcomes.text: A warm, blurry, laughing evening. Everyone left glowing.
The conversation turned nasty at midnight. Someone left in tears.
A gentle wind-down. The chat got deeper.
A few people were disappointed. Most were relieved.
Awkward but safe. People understood.
They thought I was being rude. A week of messages.

title: Passed around
text: At a house party, a bag is going round the room. When it reaches you, everyone's looking at you without looking at you.

outcomes.text: An hour of pure wonder, then a long grey comedown. I was frightened by how much I'd liked it.
Nothing happened for ages, then everything did. I was sick in the garden.
Nobody minded. A girl at the end said, 'Smart.' I found I agreed.
I felt out of place for the rest of the night, but proud of it.
I walked home under streetlights, a bit shaky and a bit free.
I phoned my mum from the bus stop. We chatted for an hour.

title: The brownie
text: Someone has made a tray of brownies. 'Special ones,' they say quietly. You've had one. It's been forty minutes and you feel nothing, and the tray looks very tempting.

outcomes.text: Eventually it hit. I spent two hours staring at a lamp, utterly content.
It hit hard. I thought the sofa was breathing.
A terrible idea. I spent the night hugging a bin.
I discovered several things I love about cheese.
I woke up fine and slightly embarrassed.
It hit at 3 a.m. in bed. A strange and blissful hour.

title: Someone at the door
text: A friend of a friend has turned up at your flat, polite, with a small bag. 'First one's free,' he says. 'For the friend of a friend.'

outcomes.text: Free things are never free. A month later, I owed him.
It was fine. I wanted more. That was the problem.
He shrugged and left. It was so easy that I was annoyed with myself for being scared.
He came back. I called a friend who dealt with it.
I did the right thing. I also looked over my shoulder for months.
They came and found nothing. He'd gone. I felt silly and safe.

title: Not breathing right
text: At 4 a.m. your friend is grey and slumped against the wall, breathing slow and shallow, and everyone else has gone very still.

outcomes.text: They came in eight minutes. He lived. The doctor said, 'You saved him.' I didn't feel like it.
Everyone ran. I stayed, and so did he. He lived. We both changed.
He came round after a long minute, groggy and ashamed. We never discussed it.
He didn't. I phoned the ambulance, too late to matter much, and he was in hospital for days.
I never knew what happened. I think about it all the time.
Someone else called. He lived. I didn't speak to anyone for a week.

title: Focus
text: A colleague slips you a small packet at lunch. 'Just for the deadline. It'll change your life.'

outcomes.text: Three days of terrifying focus. I finished everything and couldn't sleep for a week.
I rushed through the work and made mistakes I didn't notice.
I stayed up the old way, with coffee. It was exhausting and clean.
I told HR later. They thanked me and handled it quietly.
It was handled discreetly. My colleague transferred. I felt both right and cold.
They didn't believe me. Awkward months followed.

title: The shakes
text: Three days without, and your hands won't hold a cup. The ceiling is crawling. The phone is at your elbow with a number you know by heart.

outcomes.text: A bad week. I came out thin and clear.
I lasted two days and gave in, ashamed.
A clinic took me in. It was gentle and terrifying and right.
A helpline picked up at 4 a.m. and stayed on for an hour.
It made the shaking stop. It didn't make anything else stop.
It was a relief and an ending.

title: Six months clean
text: There's a small white chip in your palm and a room full of folding chairs. They're clapping and you don't know where to put your hands.

outcomes.text: I said six sentences and sat down shaking. People wept. So did I.
I said one. It was enough.
A small beautiful moment, privately mine.
Someone sat next to me and said nothing. It meant everything.
Pride and fear. I came back next week.
I wasn't ready. I came back eventually.

title: After the surgery
text: The prescription is generous. Two weeks later the pain has gone but the pills have not, and the bottle on the bedside table is nearly empty.

outcomes.text: A slow, careful taper. I felt each dose go and I was fine.
It was harder than I'd thought. The doctor stuck with me.
She gave one, with a look. I took more than I should.
She refused. I found another source.
A bad few days. A clear mind after.
I hadn't needed them for a week. I'd been scared of the pain.

title: A friend slipping
text: Your oldest friend has been missing plans, borrowing money, and looking at the wall when you speak to them. You think you know why.

outcomes.text: They broke down. We spent the night talking. They agreed to see someone.
They denied everything, and cut me off for a while. Later they apologised.
It went exactly where I feared. I felt used.
It helped them get through a bad week. I never knew where it went.
It was self-protection. I mourned a bit.
They got better, eventually, without me. I don't know how I feel.

title: Festival field
text: Three days in a field with a hundred thousand strangers. Someone hands you a tiny paper square. 'It's going to be a beautiful night.'

outcomes.text: The night was a river of stars. I laughed until sunrise. I also didn't sleep for two days.
It went wrong. A medic tent and a very kind stranger.
I danced anyway, clear-eyed. Best festival ever.
I spent the night at the back, watching. Fine.
I forgot about it. I found it in my sock a week later and threw it away.
My bag was searched at the exit. The paper was in my pocket.

title: A search at the gate
text: Security have asked to look in your bag. At the bottom, in a paper envelope you'd forgotten, is something you shouldn't have brought.

outcomes.text: A caution, a lecture and a very polite officer. I walked away shaken and grateful.
A fine and a warning. It could have been much worse.
They didn't believe me. It was awkward, and then it was serious.
A friend took the blame. I owe them forever.
I made it. My heart is still thumping from that.
A barrier stopped me. It got messy.

title: The wet bend
text: The road bends left and the car does not. For one long second there is nothing but a hedge, a ditch and your own breath.

outcomes.text: The tyres bit. The car came straight. I stopped on the verge and shook for twenty minutes.
It spun once, slowly, and stopped facing the way I'd come. I was completely unharmed.
The car spun and hit the bank. Airbags, a cracked rib, a write-off.
The car slid sideways and clipped a post. A very expensive scrape.
When I opened them the car was in a field. Intact. I don't know how.
I woke in an ambulance. I was lucky.

title: Smoke on the stairs
text: You wake at 3 a.m. to a smell you can't place and a noise that isn't the cat. The landing is full of grey smoke.

outcomes.text: I woke everyone and we stood on the pavement in pyjamas watching the engines arrive. It could have been far worse.
We got out. The house didn't recover. We lost almost everything.
I went back for the photo albums and nearly didn't make it out. The albums survived.
I got the dog and the laptop. It was a stupid risk.
The call took sixty seconds. They were here in six minutes. The fire was out by four.
The line was busy. I counted to ten and tried again.

title: The rip
text: You swam out further than you meant to. When you turn, the shore is a long, thin line and the water is taking you sideways.

outcomes.text: It took twenty minutes. I crawled up the sand, shaking and humble.
A lifeguard's board arrived just as my arms gave out.
I swallowed seawater and made no progress. Someone threw me a ring.
I almost didn't make it. A stranger dragged me in.
Rescued in four minutes. It looked silly, and I'd do it again.
Nobody saw. I floated for a long hour until I was close enough.

title: The tightness
text: It starts as a heaviness behind the breastbone while carrying shopping. Then your left arm goes strange, and you sit down on a bench, very carefully.

outcomes.text: It was a heart attack, caught early. They stented me within the hour.
It was a panic attack. The paramedic was kind. I felt foolish and relieved.
It passed. I told no one. I was lucky.
It got worse. A passer-by dialled for me. I owe that stranger my life.
She took one look and called an ambulance. Strict, quick, right.
She wasn't in. I sat in the waiting room and nearly fainted.

title: A restaurant, a silence
text: Across the table, your companion has stopped mid-sentence. Their hand goes to their throat and their eyes widen. Nobody else has noticed.

outcomes.text: Three thrusts and a piece of steak shot across the room. The restaurant applauded.
Four attempts. It worked on the last. I've never had my heart beat like that.
A chef ran over and saved them. I stood there feeling useless.
Someone who knew what to do stepped in, calm as anything.
A waiter acted first. I thought about that moment for a long time.
The moment passed and they coughed it out themselves. I will never forgive myself for freezing.

title: The wrong ridge
text: The cloud came down faster than the forecast said. The path has vanished, your phone shows no signal, and it will be dark in two hours.

outcomes.text: Mountain rescue found me by torchlight at nine. I'd never been so glad to see an orange jacket.
I stayed put. A shepherd found me in the morning, sipping tea from my flask.
It led to a farm. A warm kitchen and a lot of explaining.
It led to a ravine. I clung to a rock for an hour before climbing out.
I made the road at midnight, scratched, cold, alive.
I fell. A broken ankle, two cold nights, and a very good helicopter.

title: A reaction
text: A mouthful in, your lips tingle. Your tongue is swelling, your throat feels thick, and the dessert on your fork has nuts in it, you realise.

outcomes.text: It worked within minutes. My heart raced, my hands shook, and I lived.
I didn't have one. A stranger did. I'll never forget the face.
They were quick. Adrenaline, a drip and an overnight stay.
They were slow. It was the worst fifteen minutes of my life.
It eased. I was stupidly lucky.
It didn't ease. I was hospitalised for three days.

title: The alley
text: Walking home, a voice behind you says 'Wallet.' The word is quiet and the thing against your back is not a finger.

outcomes.text: He took it and ran. I stood and shook. The money was replaceable; I was fine.
He took it and my phone. I called the police from a shop.
I got a cut on the arm and he got my wallet anyway. It was a bad idea.
I surprised him. He ran. I sat on the kerb and laughed hysterically.
I ran until my lungs burned. He didn't follow.
He tripped me. A bad fall, a broken wrist.

title: The scan
text: The consultant has put the scan on the light box. For a long moment nobody speaks, and then she turns the chair around.

outcomes.text: It was serious, but treatable. A long road, but with a map.
It was benign. I laughed in the corridor until I cried.

choices.label: Bring someone with you next time

outcomes.text: My sister held my hand through every appointment. We got through it together.
I couldn't ask. I went alone. It was lonely.
A second doctor agreed with the first, but offered a better plan.
A second doctor found the first had been wrong. Nobody said sorry.

title: Wrong side of the window
text: You wake up on the balcony in your nightclothes, two floors up, with one leg over the rail and no memory of how you got there.

outcomes.text: My heart nearly burst. I locked the door and told no one for a month.
I woke my flatmate. We both sat in the kitchen until dawn.
A neighbour came. She held me by the belt until the police arrived.
Nobody heard. I got myself back.
A sleep study found the cause. The treatment worked.
They found nothing. I installed a lock on the balcony.

title: The platform edge
text: You drop your phone at the platform's edge, the express is a mile off and the lights are rushing, and your fingers are already reaching.

outcomes.text: The train came through and the phone was dust. I breathed for a full minute.
A man grabbed my arm. 'Not worth it,' he said, and bought me a coffee.
I made it back with a second to spare. I've never been so stupid or so lucky.
It was very close. I was shaken for weeks.

choices.label: Shout and wave at the driver

outcomes.text: The driver braked. Nobody was hurt, and everyone stared.
He didn't see. The phone was crushed.

title: A new virus
text: The news has gone from a footnote to a headline in a week. The shelves are bare, and your neighbour is coughing in a way you don't like.

outcomes.text: Weeks of quiet, bread-baking and boredom. We were fine.
Lockdown cabin fever. The walls moved in.
I caught it. A week in bed, a month of fatigue.
I was fine. I felt reckless and relieved.
I delivered food to neighbours. I felt useful, and scared.
I caught it from a delivery. I recovered but I'm not the same.

title: The floor moves
text: The coffee cup walks across the table. Then the building begins to groan, and the ceiling light swings in great slow arcs.

outcomes.text: Thirty seconds that lasted a year. When it stopped, nobody was hurt.
A bookcase fell where I'd been standing. I stared at it for an hour.
I made it to the street and dodged a falling sign. Dumb luck.
Glass fell like rain. I was cut, but alive.
I pulled a neighbour from a doorway. I'll never forget their face.
I pulled them out and went back for another. It was a long night.

title: Water in the house
text: It rained for nine days. The river has stopped being a river and started being a lake, and the water is at the second step.

outcomes.text: The water stopped at the fourth step. We lost the ground floor and nothing else.
It rose to the ceiling downstairs. We were rescued by boat.
We left with a bag each and a photo album. The house was never the same.
The road was already gone. We went by a neighbour's tractor.
We held it all night. A brilliant, hopeless, beautiful fight.
It rose over the bags at 4 a.m. We lost.

title: The same car again
text: It's the third night you've seen the same dark car at the end of the road, engine off, someone sitting inside.

outcomes.text: They found a man with a grievance and a camera. He was warned off. I slept badly for weeks.
They found nothing. I changed my routine for a month.
It was a private detective. He'd been hired by someone I knew. It took years to untangle.
They drove off. The car never came back.
Two of us watched from the window the following night. Nobody came.
My friend thought I was paranoid. I wasn't.

title: A dare in the shop
text: Your friends have bet you can walk out with the biggest chocolate bar. The security guard is looking at his phone.

outcomes.text: I got away with it. The thrill lasted an hour. The sick feeling lasted a week.
The guard grabbed my collar. His face was very close. My mother had to pick me up.
They groaned. I ate it in front of them, legally.
They laughed. I laughed. It was a good chocolate bar.
They called me boring. It stung for a day.
One of them followed. He wanted out too.

title: The mug on the desk
text: Your boss has just spoken to you in front of the entire office as though you were furniture. Your hand is already closing around your mug.

outcomes.text: I walked out into the sunshine feeling like a hero. By Friday I felt like a fool.
I walked out. Two colleagues followed. We founded something later.
It worked. The boss apologised, awkwardly, in the kitchen.
It did not. I was told to take a few days.
I stayed quiet and burned inside for weeks.
I wrote an angry email and deleted it. It was cathartic.

title: The card on the sofa
text: It's 1 a.m. You have a card, a sale and a feeling. The basket total says $1,240 and the 'buy now' button looks inviting.

outcomes.text: The parcels came in waves. I returned half and kept the rest. I felt guilty about the other half.
It all arrived and I didn't like any of it.
I woke up relieved. The sale had ended. So had the urge.
I thought about it for three days. Then I bought one thing.
A dramatic gesture. A sensible one.
I cut it up, then ordered a new one the next day.

title: I wasn't supposed to say that
text: A friend told you something in confidence. Now, three drinks in, a group is laughing, and the secret is on your tongue like a coin.

outcomes.text: Nobody ever knew. My friend and I were closer for it.
I kept it. It was heavy.
It spread. My friend found out. It ended the friendship.
It got round. Something awful happened. I regretted it forever.
They guessed. They never said I told them.
They guessed, and told my friend that I'd hinted. I got a stern text.

title: A little embellishment
text: The application form asks for 'degree'. You don't have one. You have three-quarters of a degree and a great deal of confidence.

outcomes.text: I got the interview and the job. I lived in fear for years.
A background check caught it. I was dropped on the spot.
They were impressed by the candour. I got an interview.
They filtered me out. It stung.
'Degree-level study.' It worked, and it was true.
They asked about it. I stumbled.

title: The appointment you cancel
text: The surgery has called to remind you of your check-up. You've got a meeting. You've got a lot going on. You cancel it, for the third time.

outcomes.text: I went. It was fine. I felt silly for putting it off.
I went. They found something small, early, easily dealt with.
A year later, a minor problem was a bigger one.
Nothing came of it. I got away with it.

choices.label: Go, but lie about your habits

outcomes.text: The doctor smelled it on me anyway.
It all came out. I felt scolded and cared for.

title: Leaving them on read
text: A friend who had a bad year has sent three messages. You've read them all. They're sitting there, unanswered, like a stone in a shoe.

outcomes.text: It was awkward at first, and then lovely. I should've done it sooner.
They'd moved on, kindly. I felt a pang.
A week passed. Then a month. We drifted.
A year passed. I met them at a funeral. They hugged me.
A clean break. I felt strange about it for years.
I deleted it. They noticed.

title: Flash in the mirror
text: A white flash in the rear mirror and the sinking certainty of a camera. It said forty on the sign, and you were doing fifty-eight.

outcomes.text: A clean, painless payment. A reminder to be kinder to my foot.
It came with penalty points. A fortnight of careful driving.
It was thrown out on a technicality. I danced in the kitchen.
I lost, and paid the full amount plus costs.
A reminder arrived. Then a bigger one. Then a court date.
It vanished. I'll never know why.

title: Post in haste
text: After a nasty row, you've written a long, devastating post about the person involved. The cursor hovers over 'publish'.

outcomes.text: It got a hundred likes and a hundred regrets. I lost a friend and gained an enemy.
It went viral. People took sides, and I wasn't winning.
In the morning, it read like a stranger's anger. I deleted it.
In the morning, I still meant it, but I knew better.

choices.label: Send it only to a friend

outcomes.text: She read it, sighed, and said 'don't'. She was right.
It leaked. I wasn't happy.

title: A can't-lose opportunity
text: An old schoolfriend turns up with a glossy brochure, a new car and a very white smile. 'Honestly, it's not a pyramid. It's a community.'

outcomes.text: I recruited three people, lost two friends, and made $40. I lost $1,200.
I was out within a month, a little poorer and a lot wiser.
I looked it up. It was a pyramid. I warned others.
They were offended. It got awkward.
Two hours of clapping, then a pitch. I left politely.
I almost bought in. A friend dragged me out.

title: Can you lend me...
text: A friend has asked for a loan. 'Just until payday.' It's not a small amount. Their payday has a track record.

outcomes.text: They paid me back, a month late, with a bottle of wine. It was fine.
They didn't. They vanished. A friendship, bought for $800.
A smaller sum. They were thankful. No hard feelings.
They were offended by the smaller sum.
It was awkward. It would have been worse.
They stopped talking to me. I decided I could live with that.

title: Cut up
text: A van cuts you off at the roundabout and the driver gives you a gesture. Something in you quietly snaps.

outcomes.text: I chased him half across town. He pulled over and got out. He was bigger than the van.
I lost him. I sat in a lay-by shaking, ashamed of myself.
I put on a song. It was a good one.
I pulled over for five minutes and called a friend.
I felt great for ten seconds. Then a passenger in my car said 'wow.'
It got me nothing. It cost me a little pride.

title: A message you shouldn't have sent
text: It's a flirt, nothing more. The reply came quickly and was a lot more than flirting. Your thumb is on the next reply.

outcomes.text: It went further than I meant. It cost me a relationship.
It was exciting and sordid. My partner found out in a week.
A close call. I felt ashamed, and kinder to my partner for a while.
I deleted it. I still thought about it.
It was the hardest conversation we ever had. We came out the other side.
They were hurt, and furious, and stayed.

title: Not your car
text: Your friend's car keys are on the table. He's asleep upstairs. There is a late-night shop two miles away with a certain snack.

outcomes.text: Two miles, a snack, home. Nobody ever knew. I've never felt so guilty about chips.
I clipped a bollard. The car had a dent. He thought it had been like that.
A pleasant midnight walk. Worth it.
It was raining. I regretted it.
He grumbled, then came with me. A mini road trip.
He grumbled. I stayed hungry.

title: Reselling
text: You've got tickets to a sold-out concert and a reseller is offering four times face value. You're not sure the buyer is legitimate.

outcomes.text: A tidy profit and a fine evening. Nobody was hurt.
It was a scam on their side: a fake payment. I lost both the tickets and the money.
It was one of the best nights of my life.
